brief: Goldman's midday color: risk-off dominates, with major indices ranked RTY > SPX > NDX, VIX near a 30-handle, and GS's Panic Index at 9/10. Breadth is poor: 60% of SPX names are red after 464 closed down the prior session. Despite a 10bp pullback in rates, GS's financial-conditions index keeps tightening. Tech leads the selloff: GS's AI basket -6.5%, Semis -7.6%, Software -1.2%, NVDA -6.8% (down 9 of the past 10 sessions). GS says investors had hoped ECM issuance would clear the way for a year-end risk-back-on trade; without it, the pullback has been harder to absorb. Defensives outperform (staples +1.6%, utilities +1.2%) while cyclicals-vs-defensives is -2.8%, and retail-favorites and bitcoin-sensitive baskets are down 6.6% and 7%. CTAs have sold $57bn over the past month, are net short $19bn, and are modeled to sell $28.6bn-$80.6bn more next week by tape direction. Liquidity is thin (top-of-book depth $1.5mm, lowest since Liberation Day) and ETF volumes are 39% of tape, highest since March. GS's own flows skew 1% toward selling even as long-onlys and hedge funds skew toward buying. The SPX is on track for a 7th straight lower close, rare over recent decades.
